item.title: WNBA Finals Game 1 preview: Atlanta’s +19 pressure meets Golden State’s +23 rebounding
item.dc:creator: Ryan Moalemi
item.description: The Dream and Valkyries open the WNBA Finals on Saturday, Oct. 17, at 12:30 PM PT. Updated Oct. 15, 2026.
item.content:encoded:
WNBA PlayoffsFull Court Buckets

WNBA Finals Game 1 preview: Atlanta’s +19 pressure meets Golden State’s +23 rebounding

By Ryan MoalemiOctober 10, 2026

This preview was published before the game. For the result, read our game recap. 2026 WNBA Finals ratings tracker.

Atlanta reached the WNBA Finals by forcing turnovers. Golden State kept winning by collecting its own misses.

The Dream forced 49 turnovers in their semifinal sweep of New York while committing 30. The Valkyries committed more turnovers than Las Vegas but outrebounded the Aces 37–14 on the offensive glass. Those extra chances helped Golden State finish its own sweep.

That sets up the central question for Game 1: Can Atlanta protect the ball and finish defensive possessions with a rebound?

The Finals begin Saturday, Oct. 17, at Chase Center. Golden State swept the regular-season series, but the teams last met in July. Both arrive playing their best basketball, and one will leave this series with its first championship.

Finals Game 1 at a glance

  • When: Saturday, Oct. 17, at 12:30 p.m. PT
  • Where: Chase Center, San Francisco
  • TV and streaming: NBC and Peacock
  • Format: Best of seven, with a 2-2-1-1-1 home schedule
  • Home-court advantage: Golden State

Full Finals schedule

  • Game 1: Saturday, Oct. 17, 3:30 p.m. ET / 12:30 p.m. PT, Chase Center, NBC and Peacock
  • Game 2: Monday, Oct. 19, 8:00 p.m. ET / 5:00 p.m. PT, Chase Center, USA, CNBC and Peacock
  • Game 3: Wednesday, Oct. 21, 8:00 p.m. ET / 5:00 p.m. PT, State Farm Arena, USA, CNBC and Peacock
  • Game 4: Saturday, Oct. 24, 1:00 p.m. ET / 10:00 a.m. PT, State Farm Arena, NBC and Peacock
  • Games 5, 6 and 7: Not listed in the Oct. 13, 2026 WNBA release. If necessary.

Games 1 through 4 follow the WNBA release of Oct. 13, 2026. That release does not list dates, tip times, or networks for Games 5, 6 and 7.

Injury report

Updated Oct. 15, 2026: an earlier version of this preview said Allisha Gray was expected back for Game 1.

As of Oct. 15, 2026, Allisha Gray is day-to-day after a minor procedure on her left hand. She was a limited participant in practice Thursday with her left ring and pinky fingers taped, and she is hopeful to play in Game 1. The medical staff will make the final call.

An Oct. 9 listing had her out with a left-hand injury for the semifinal finale against New York. That entry does not set her status for Finals Game 1.

Before that semifinal game, coach Karl Smesko said: “She's making good progress since her injury. In the interest of caution, they ruled her out for today.”

Brionna Jones is out for the season with a left-leg injury.

Golden State: Iliana Rupert, out for the season for a non-injury reason, is the only player listed.

How they got here

Atlanta finished the regular season 30–14 as the No. 4 seed and is 5–0 in the playoffs after sweeping Washington and New York. The Dream have won a franchise-best 10 straight games and are making their fourth Finals appearance. Their previous trips, in 2010, 2011 and 2013, all ended in sweeps.

Golden State went 32–12 to earn the No. 2 seed. The Valkyries are 5–1 in the postseason after beating Dallas in three games and sweeping Las Vegas, closing the semifinals with an 87–77 overtime win. They are the fastest expansion team to reach the Finals, getting there in their second season.

Golden State won the regular-season meetings 77–66 and 78–75 at Chase Center, then 88–83 in Atlanta. Those wins came by a combined 19 points, with the last on July 4. Atlanta has lost only once since its Aug. 18 win at Las Vegas.

Golden State’s last win over Atlanta came on July 4, before the Dream’s current 10-game winning streak began.

Neither team has played since Oct. 9, giving both seven full days off before the opener.

The battle for extra chances

Atlanta’s semifinal turnover advantage translated into a 72–31 edge in points off turnovers. That is where Golden State needs to be careful: the Valkyries committed 40 turnovers against Las Vegas while forcing 33.

Golden State survived that deficit by repeatedly extending possessions. Its 23-rebound advantage on the offensive glass gave the Aces more defensive work and the Valkyries more opportunities to score.

Combining turnover differential and offensive-rebound differential gives Atlanta a margin of plus-28 in the semifinals and Golden State plus-16. That is a rough comparison of two ways to create extra chances, not a count of total possessions. The teams also faced different opponents, so those margins describe how they won rather than predict this matchup.

Angel Reese and Kiah Stokes will be central to the rebounding contest. On the perimeter, Jordin Canada and Rhyne Howard face Gabby Williams and Veronica Burton.

Stokes called the Finals “a clean slate.” Golden State has already shown it can beat Atlanta, but the Dream’s recent ball pressure gives the Valkyries a specific problem to solve.

Golden State’s bench advantage

The Valkyries’ reserves outscored Las Vegas’s bench 88–34 in the semifinals. Atlanta’s bench held a smaller 52–40 advantage over New York.

Gray played only 11 minutes in the series. As of Oct. 15, 2026, she is day-to-day and hopeful to play in Game 1, with the medical staff making the final call. Her return could change Atlanta’s rotation and reduce the burden on its other scorers. Her availability alone would not erase Golden State’s depth advantage.

Both teams have already handled tight finishes. Atlanta won one semifinal game by three in overtime and another by two. Golden State’s final two wins came by two points and in overtime.

The odds and my pick

The listed DraftKings Game 1 line has Golden State favored by 2.5 points, with a total of 153.5. Atlanta is +114 on the moneyline and Golden State is -135.

BetMGM’s series prices are nearly even: Valkyries -115 and Dream -105. These are the prices recorded for this preview; they may change.

My pick is Atlanta to win Game 1, with Dream +2.5 as my betting lean.

Atlanta protected the ball against New York and consistently turned the Liberty’s mistakes into points. Golden State committed more turnovers than it forced against Las Vegas. Golden State was minus-7 in turnovers against Las Vegas, and Atlanta was plus-19 against New York. That gives the Dream an opening on the road.

The concern is the glass. Forcing a turnover helps little if Atlanta gives those opportunities back through offensive rebounds. The Dream need Reese and the rest of the lineup to finish defensive possessions, particularly when Stokes keeps a missed shot alive.

This lean does not assume Gray sits. Check her confirmed status and the current line before betting.

21+. Gamble responsibly. 1-800-GAMBLER.

TV: NBC · Stream: Peacock

item.title: Allisha Gray Is Out for Game 3 as the Dream Go for the Sweep in Brooklyn
item.dc:creator: Ryan Moalemi
item.description: Allisha Gray is out for Game 3. The Dream will try to sweep the Liberty without their leading scorer.
item.content:encoded:
WNBA PlayoffsFull Court Buckets

Allisha Gray Is Out for Game 3 as the Dream Go for the Sweep in Brooklyn

By Ryan MoalemiOctober 9, 2026

Allisha Gray is out for Game 3. She took part in shootaround Friday and was a game-time decision as recently as early afternoon, but the Atlanta Dream will try to sweep the New York Liberty without their leading scorer. Atlanta won Game 1 with Gray on the floor for just 11 minutes. And there's a date on ESPN's report that tells you what the Dream are hoping for.

Updated 3:45 PM PT, Friday, Oct. 9

What we know

  • ESPN's injury report now lists Gray as out with a left hand injury, updated at 3:21 PM PT. It shows an estimated return date of Oct. 11. That's Sunday, the day of Game 4 in New York if this series gets there (WNBA.com).
  • Yahoo Sports' live blog reported Gray out for Game 3 at 3:22 PM PT (Yahoo Sports).
  • Earlier Friday, ESPN's Alexa Philippou said she saw Gray in shootaround with something stabilizing her finger and that Gray would go through warmups before the Dream decided (ClutchPoints, 1:01 PM PT).

Why she matters

Gray led the Dream at 19.0 points a game this season and averaged 22.0 in their first-round sweep of Washington (ESPN). In Game 1 she had 7 points in 11 minutes, going 1-of-5 from the field and 4-of-5 at the line, before hurting her shooting hand.

Atlanta won anyway. 92-82 in Game 1 with Gray out from late in the first half, then 101-98 in overtime in Game 2 without her at all.

What it means tonight

My take: this hurts less than it should. The Dream have won this series on turnovers, offensive boards and Angel Reese, not on Gray's scoring. I still like Atlanta to finish it tonight. If it slips, that Sunday return date starts looking pretty important.

item.title: Semis Game 3 Preview: Can the Liberty and Aces Do What No WNBA Team Has Done?
item.dc:creator: Ryan Moalemi
item.description: Teams up 2-0 in a best-of-five WNBA series are 19-0. Turnovers sink the Liberty, rebounds sink the Aces. Picks for both Game 3s on Friday.
item.content:encoded:
WNBA PlayoffsFull Court Buckets

Semis Game 3 Preview: Can the Liberty and Aces Do What No WNBA Team Has Done?

By Ryan MoalemiOctober 9, 2026

This preview was published before the games. For the results, read our recaps: Dream sweep the Liberty and Valkyries sweep the Aces.

New York has outscored Atlanta in four of the eight regulation quarters and still trails the series 2-0. The difference is possessions: the Liberty have committed 38 turnovers to the Dream's 22, and Atlanta has taken 26 more shots across the two games.

Both semifinal Game 3s are Friday, and the stakes are simple. Teams that take a 2-0 lead in a best-of-five WNBA series are 19-0 all time. The Liberty and the Las Vegas Aces are both trying to be the first team to come back.

Late news (updated Oct 9, 3:45 PM PT)

  • Dream: Allisha Gray (left hand) is out for Game 3 per ESPN's injury report, updated at 3:21 PM PT, with an estimated return of Oct 11.
  • Liberty: We found no announced lineup change as of 2:10 PM PT.
  • Aces: Jewell Loyd and Stephanie Talbot (left leg) are still listed as game-time decisions on ESPN's injury report. Talbot's entry was updated at 12:05 PM PT. Dana Evans isn't on the list.
  • Valkyries: No new injuries. Only Iliana Rupert, out for the season, is listed.
  • Lines moved: Liberty -3.5 (was -2.5), total 170.5 (was 172.5). Aces -5.5 (was -3.5), total 156.5 (unchanged). DraftKings via ESPN, checked at 2:04 PM PT.

Dream at Liberty: Friday, 4:30 PM PT, Barclays Center, ESPN2

What decided Games 1 and 2. Ball security, both nights. New York has turned it over 38 times in two games, counting team turnovers. Atlanta has 22. The Dream have scored 60 points off those giveaways while the Liberty have scored 24. That's a 36-point swing in a series Atlanta leads by a combined 13.

Atlanta also leads 20-12 in offensive rebounds and 155-129 in field goal attempts. New York has shot better, 48.8% to 42.6%, but that advantage has not made up for the gap in attempts. The Dream lead 29-8 in fast-break points, too.

The key matchup. Angel Reese against that New York frontcourt. Reese is plus-18 in the series, the best mark on either team, with Jordin Canada at plus-17 and Naz Hillmon at plus-16. On the other side, Marine Fauthoux is the only Liberty player with a positive plus-minus (plus-6). Starters Leonie Fiebich and Pauline Astier are both minus-10.

These plus-minus figures cover only two games and reflect the lineups on the floor. They help describe what happened; they do not isolate any one player's impact.

New York's stars are scoring. Breanna Stewart dropped 35 in Game 2 and Sabrina Ionescu had 27 in Game 1. But Ionescu also had 5 turnovers in Game 1, and Jonquel Jones had 6 in Game 2.

Atlanta's bench has outscored New York's 42-29, and 23 of those came from DeWanna Bonner in Game 1. And they did most of this without their leading scorer. Gray hurt her left shooting hand in Game 1, played 11 minutes and missed Game 2. She is out for Game 3 per ESPN's injury report, updated 3:21 PM PT, with an estimated return of Oct 11.

New York needs to protect the ball and finish defensive possessions with a rebound. Its shooting has kept both games competitive; fewer empty trips would give that shooting a better chance to matter. Atlanta can keep pressing the advantage by forcing turnovers and pursuing second chances.

My pick is Atlanta. New York has committed at least 17 turnovers in each game, and the Dream have repeatedly converted those mistakes into points. Allisha Gray's availability could strengthen that pick, but Atlanta has already shown it can win without her.

Valkyries at Aces: Friday, 6:30 PM PT, Michelob ULTRA Arena, Peacock and NBCSN

What decided Games 1 and 2. The glass. The Golden State Valkyries have 27 offensive rebounds to Vegas's 8, and they've outrebounded the Aces 82-50. Rebounds here use the player totals in the linked box score. Kiah Stokes hasn't scored a point in this series and still has 21 rebounds.

Then there's the bench. Golden State's reserves have outscored Vegas's 61-21. Tiffany Hayes has 24 of those, including 21 in 17 minutes in Game 2. Janelle Salaun is plus-18 in just 10 minutes, and Kaitlyn Chen is plus-11.

Here's the stat that should scare Golden State. The Valkyries have turned it over 29 times to Vegas's 18, counting team turnovers. They're winning anyway because Vegas hasn't punished it, scoring 24 points off those turnovers to Golden State's 27.

The key matchup. Golden State's starts against Vegas's finishes. The Valkyries are plus-14 in first halves. In second halves, the Aces are plus-1. Golden State won the first quarter of Game 2 by 8, and Vegas answered by winning the fourth by 9.

A'ja Wilson has 48 points in two games and is still minus-11. Chelsea Gray is also minus-11. The Aces' best plus-minus belongs to Kalani Brown at plus-7, while Brianna Turner is minus-16 and Kierstan Bell is minus-15.

Injuries matter here. As of Friday afternoon, ESPN still listed Loyd and Talbot as game-time decisions with left leg injuries. Loyd didn't play in Game 2. Evans wasn't on ESPN's injury list when we checked, and she played 18 minutes in Game 2.

What each team has to do. Vegas has to box out. You can't give up 17 offensive rebounds like they did in Game 1 and survive. Golden State has to clean up the turnovers and get the same punch from Gabby Williams, who has 45 points in two games, and Kayla Thornton.

The pick: Aces win Game 3. The defending champs, who beat Phoenix 4-0 in the 2025 Finals, won the second half of this series, swept the regular-season meetings 3-0, and get Michelob ULTRA Arena behind them. In Game 2 they outshot Golden State 44% to 41% and had the ball down two at the end. If Wilson and Gray stop digging out of holes, Vegas extends this. If the Aces lose the glass 52-25 like they did in Game 1, nothing else matters.

For the bettors and fantasy players

The home teams were favored for Game 3. These DraftKings prices, displayed by ESPN at 2:04 p.m. PT on October 9, are for the individual games, not the series: Liberty -3.5 and Aces -5.5. That's a bold call, because the Dream and Valkyries are both 2-0 against the spread. The totals sit at 170.5 and 156.5. Both Dream-Liberty games went over, while Valkyries-Aces split 1-1.

Across Games 1 and 2, Breanna Stewart averaged 51.6 DraftKings points and Gabby Williams averaged 40.8. Tiffany Hayes produced 36.75 points in 28 total minutes. Her per-36 rate describes a small sample; it is not a minutes or scoring projection. My betting leans are Dream +3.5 and the Aces moneyline. Allisha Gray is out for Game 3 per ESPN's injury report, updated 3:21 PM PT, with an estimated return of Oct 11. Check the latest injury report and prices before placing a bet. 21+. Gamble responsibly. 1-800-GAMBLER.

Dream at Liberty: TV: ESPN2 · Stream: Fubo, Hulu + Live TV. Valkyries at Aces: Stream: Peacock · TV: NBCSN

item.title: Valkyries beat Aces 87-77 in overtime to sweep their way into the WNBA Finals
item.dc:creator: Ryan Moalemi
item.description: The Valkyries beat the Aces 87-77 in overtime in Las Vegas to sweep the semifinals and reach the WNBA Finals.
item.content:encoded:
WNBA PlayoffsFull Court Buckets

Valkyries beat Aces 87-77 in overtime to sweep their way into the WNBA Finals

By Ryan MoalemiOctober 9, 2026

The Golden State Valkyries are going to the WNBA Finals. They beat the Las Vegas Aces 87-77 in overtime in Las Vegas on Friday, and the play that broke it open was Gabby Williams hitting an 18-foot step-back with 54.7 seconds left in OT to make it 81-73. Golden State won overtime 16-6 and finished off a 3-0 sweep of a team that had beaten them all three times in the regular season.

How the Valkyries got back in it

Vegas controlled the first half. The Aces won the second quarter 26-20 and went to the locker room up 45-36.

The third quarter flipped it. Golden State outscored Vegas 17-7, and the Aces scored just seven points in 10 minutes in an elimination game at home. After three it was 53-52 Golden State.

The fourth went back and forth, and Vegas looked like it had it. The Aces led 69-63 when Veronica Burton went to the line at 2:51 and made both, making it 69-65. Then the Valkyries defense took over.

  • 2:17: Kiah Stokes layup off a Williams feed, 69-67.
  • 1:54: Williams stripped A'ja Wilson, and Kayla Thornton finished a running layup off Williams' pass at 1:50 to tie it at 69.
  • 1:12: Burton hit a 9-footer for a 71-69 lead.
  • 56.8: Stokes picked off a Jackie Young pass.
  • 28.6: Stokes blocked Wilson's driving layup.

Vegas still found an answer. Young scored off a Chelsea Gray assist at 26.6 to tie it at 71. Williams missed a driving layup with 5 seconds left, Gray missed a 14-foot pull-up at the horn, and we went to overtime.

Overtime

Tiffany Hayes opened the scoring with a driving layup at 4:26. Williams made a driving layup at 2:44 for 75-71. Gray's layup at 2:24 made it 75-73, and that was the last time Vegas was within one score. Hayes scored again at 2:03 for 77-73. Williams hit two free throws at 1:28, Young was called for an offensive foul at 1:13, and then Williams hit the step-back off a Stokes assist.

The next 10 seconds ended it. Stokes blocked Young at the rim at 50.8, Williams stole Gray's pass on the next trip, and Williams made two more free throws at 46.9 for 83-73. Thornton made four free throws in the final 35 seconds to close it out.

The numbers that decided it

Turnovers. Vegas turned it over 15 times to Golden State's 10. Gray had 6 and Young had 5, and three of those came in the final two minutes of regulation or overtime.

Stokes. She went 5-for-5 from the field for 11 points with 10 rebounds, 3 blocks and 2 steals, and she was +18 in 38 minutes. Her two blocks on Wilson and Young came in the last 30 seconds of regulation and the final minute of overtime.

Wilson had to work for everything. She scored 21 with 10 rebounds and played 43 minutes, but she shot 6-for-19 and missed a 27-foot three with 28 seconds left. A make would have cut it to 85-80, still a two-possession game.

The bench. Hayes had 11 points and was +20 in 22 minutes. Thornton led Golden State with 18 points and 9 rebounds and went 6-for-7 at the line.

Williams added 16 points, 3 assists and 3 steals. She shot 6-for-16, so this wasn't a clean night for her, but she made the two biggest defensive plays of the last two minutes of regulation and the shot that broke overtime open.

Plus-minus is noisy over one game, so take Hayes' +20 as a sign the bench lineups worked on Friday, not a ranking of who matters most.

What it means

Golden State swept a team that beat them three times in the regular season. Game 1 was a double-digit win, but Game 2 came down to a block with 3 seconds left and Game 3 needed overtime. Three games is a small sample, and this series was closer than 3-0 looks.

Next up is the Atlanta Dream, who swept the New York Liberty earlier Friday with an 85-83 win in Brooklyn. The best-of-seven Finals begin Oct. 17 (WNBA.com). The WNBA Finals attendance prior record for a series is 92,599, set over five games in 2024.

My pick is the Dream in the Finals. Both teams swept, but Atlanta has protected the ball better, and Golden State turned it over more than Vegas in Games 1 and 2.
